al_grace_falls.blurb: Grace Falls is a small sport wall on the rim road of Little River Canyon, in northeast Alabama. It holds eleven bolted lines on sandstone, and nearly all of them sit in the 5.12 range, with two a notch harder, so this is a place for strong sport climbers rather than anyone warming up. The face is steep and juggy, and the far left end has a few short, bouldery lines that suit a partner with less stamina. The face tends to seep, so a stretch of dry weather makes for a far better visit. Getting to the base means a steep descent on fixed lines, which can be slick when wet. Expect quiet days compared with the bigger canyon walls.

al_turtle_rock_area_turtle_boulder.blurb: This is a single boulder cluster within the Turtle Rock section of Horse Pens 40, near Steele, Alabama, found a short way south of the neighbouring Whiplash boulders. It offers eleven sandstone problems and is gentle on the whole: most lines fall between VB and V2, a pair of V3s sit near the top of the easy group, and one far harder problem is the lone outlier. That spread makes it a friendly spot for newer boulderers, families of climbers and warm-up laps before moving on to harder blocks. The area gets partial shade, which helps on warmer days, and the Turtle Head problems draw the most traffic.

al_supa_coola_area.blurb: Supa Coola is a compact group of sandstone boulders in the central part of Horse Pens 40, near Steele, Alabama. It carries around a dozen problems that run from very easy up to V9, though the bulk are in the V0 to V3 range, with a handful of serious projects for strong climbers. Because the easy and hard lines sit side by side, mixed groups can all find something to try. Horse Pens is known for sloper-heavy sandstone, and fall and winter are the preferred seasons. The block here feels like an easy add-on to a day spent working through the middle of the park.

al_arrowhead_trail.blurb: Arrowhead Trail is a modest bouldering spot inside Monte Sano State Park, above Huntsville, Alabama. A narrow, rocky passageway about 20 to 30 feet high holds ten boulder problems and a single top-rope line. Most problems are easy to moderate, running from VB through V3, so beginners and casual boulderers can have a good time. The rock has sharp flakes, horizontal ledges and a few pockets, and some cracks are worth a careful look before reaching in. You get there on foot along the trail from the trailhead lot, roughly a mile. It is a quiet, low-key outing rather than a destination crag, so bring water and pads.

al_novak_area.blurb: The Novak Area is a small slanted boulder in Moss Rock Preserve, a popular sandstone bouldering park in Hoover on the edge of Birmingham. Eleven problems are packed onto it, with most of the good climbing found on the west face. The grades are friendly, from V0 up to V3, and the majority sit around V2, which makes it a comfortable stop for people building up or looking for a relaxed circuit. The path threads between the halves of a split boulder, then bears left down the slope. The block is easy to pair with other nearby groupings during a day in the preserve.

al_lost_roof_area.blurb: Lost Roof is a large overhanging boulder at the far end of the trail into Moss Rock Preserve, a sandstone bouldering park in Hoover, just outside Birmingham. Its eleven problems cover a wide range, starting with easy V0 warm-ups, building through the V2 to V4 middle, and finishing with a few hard roof lines up to V8. The steep block gives it a more powerful feel than the gentler boulders nearby. Because it lies at the back of the preserve, expect a longer walk and often fewer people. Both beginners and strong climbers can find a line, and the V2 and V4 problems are the most popular.

al_road_block.blurb: Road Block is a single overhung boulder in the Middle Bishop cluster of Bishop Mountain, near Huntsville, Alabama. Its eleven problems lean toward the hard side: a few easy lines at the bottom, then a long run of V3 to V6 and several steeper projects reaching V9 or V10. The block asks for interesting body positioning on its steep face. It is reached from a gravel lot by a forest trail, branching right behind the first boulder for a walk of roughly five minutes. Stronger boulderers will get the most from it, though a couple of easier problems are on hand for a warm-up.
